result.summary: The image shows a residential/mixed-use street with sidewalks on both sides but a complete lack of marked pedestrian crossing infrastructure. The environment is characterized by narrow sidewalks, utility pole obstructions, and no visible traffic control devices for pedestrians at the intersection.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross without a designated or protected space.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground intersection area

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is situated in the middle of the sidewalk, narrowing the effective walking width and creating an obstacle for those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side sidewalk in the foreground

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the corner may block the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at the corners to ensure accessibility.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with sidewalks but no marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or visible traffic control signs. Parked vehicles near the corners and uneven pavement surfaces create hazards for pedestrians, particularly those with mobility challenges.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks any painted crosswalks, making pedestrian crossing points unclear to drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the intersection of the two streets.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The absence of sloped curb transitions creates a barrier for individuals with mobility impairments or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corners of the intersection.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners obstruct the sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs near the intersection corners on both sides.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install ladder or zebra-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

result.summary: The image shows a two-lane residential street with sidewalks on both sides but a complete lack of marked pedestrian crossings or signals. Parked vehicles along the curbs create potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross in unmarked areas without clear priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection in the middle ground

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking blocks sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, especially children or those using wheelchairs.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street along the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20-30 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: A narrow residential street lined with row houses and parked cars. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the existing crosswalk markings are significantly faded, and there is a lack of formal traffic control or pedestrian signage.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk lines in the foreground are heavily worn and difficult to see, reducing driver awareness of the crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Cars parked close to the crossing area can hide pedestrians, especially children, from oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Uneven Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: Cracks and vegetation growth in the sidewalk create potential tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right foreground sidewalks

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with continental or ladder markings to increase visibility to motorists.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crossing to improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Maintenance
interventions.description: Repair cracks and remove weeds to provide a smooth, accessible walking surface.
